penalties.authority: Assistant/ Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, SRO Hubli Employees Provident Fund Organization
penalties.details: The Assistant/Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, SRO Hubli, has levied damages of ₹29,005 under Section 14B of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, for delay in making certain provident fund contribution after the due dates during the period from 2018 to 2021. The Company is in the process of remitting the said amount.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company.

penalties.authority: Assistant Commissioner of Customs Export, ACC, Mumbai Customs Zone III
penalties.details: The Assistant Commissioner of Customs (Export), ACC, Mumbai Customs Zone III, has passed a Denovo Adjudication Order-in-Original passed in the case of Gufic Lifesciences Private Limited (currently merged with Gufic Biosciences Limited), imposing a penalty of ₹25,000 under Section 117 of the Customs Act, 1962 for alleged differential duty drawback claim. Of this amount, ₹2,000 has already been paid, and the remaining balance is recoverable. The Company is in the process of filing an appeal against the order.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Appeal is filed before the Hon’ble Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, on April 14, 2025, against the Assessment Order dated March 18, 2025, passed under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income Tax Act, 1961, by the Income Tax Department for Assessment Year 2023–24. The appeal challenges the disallowance of certain deductions claimed by the Company, which were disallowed without affording the Company an adequate opportunity for explanation. The amount of demand is Rs. 11,88,88,580/-. The appeal of the Company is treated as partly-allowed.
tax_litigation.status: The Income Tax Department has filed an appeal before the Hon’ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the relief granted to the Company. The Company has filed a cross-objection before ITAT in respect of the disallowances contested. The matter is pending for hearing.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: An Appeal was filed before the Hon’ble Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, on April 14, 2025, against the Assessment Order dated March 18, 2025, passed under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income Tax Act, 1961, by the Income Tax Department (“ITD”) for Assessment Year 2023–24. The appeal challenges the disallowance of certain deductions claimed by the Company, which were disallowed without affording the Company an adequate opportunity for explanation. The amount of demand is Rs. 11,88,88,580/-. The appeal was partly-allowed, resulting in partial relief to the Company. Subsequently, the ITD has filed an appeal before the Hon’ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the relief granted to the Company.
tax_litigation.status: Pursuant to the said appellate order, the tax demand has been substantially reduced to Rs. 11,76,198/. Further, a penalty of Rs. 23,52,396/- has been levied under Section 270A(9) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (“the Act”) on account of under-reported income. Being aggrieved by the said order, the Company has preferred an appeal before Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) within the timeframe prescribed under the Act.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received Tax Demand of Rs. 4,33,36,680/- as per the computation under section 143 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 ("Act") on account of disallowance of expenditure under Section 35(1)(i) and (iv) read with Clause 20 of Tax Audit Report for the Assessment Year 2024-25.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has preferred an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeal) within the timeframe prescribed under the Act.

penalties.authority: Assistant Commissioner of State Tax - Gujarat
penalties.details: Issuance of an intimation under Section 74 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 in respect of certain discrepancies relating to the excess availment or utilisation of Input Tax Credit between various returns and statements filed for the FY 2020-2021, pursuant to which a penalty of Rs. 3,94,290/- has been levied. The Company has paid the said penalty.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had filed an appeal before the Hon'ble Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, against the Assessment Order passed under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for Assessment Year 2023-24, challenging the disallowance of certain deductions claimed by the Company. Pursuant to the appellate order, the tax demand has been substantially reduced to Rs. 11,76,198/-. The Income Tax Department has filed an appeal before the Hon'ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the relief granted to the Company.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed a cross-objection before the Hon'ble ITAT and the matter is pending for hearing.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received Tax Demand of Rs. 4,33,36,680/- as per the intimation under section 143(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 ("Act") on account of disallowance of expenditure under Section 35(1)(i) and (iv) read with Clause 20 of Tax Audit Report for the Assessment Year 2024-25. The Company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) within the prescribed timeline under the Act.

operating_notes.text: USFDA conducted a pre-approval inspection at the Indore, Madhya Pradesh facility from October 15, 2026 to October 23, 2026, resulting in 3 observations in Form FDA 483.

timeline.summary: On May 29, 2026, Gufic Biosciences reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹251.82 Cr and net profit of ₹21.90 Cr, recommending a final dividend of Re. 0.10 per share.
Gufic Biosciences Limited’s Board of Directors, led by **Ami Shah**, recommended a final dividend of ₹0.10 per equity share for FY2025-26 on May 29, 2026.
In May 2026, Gufic Biosciences approved an investment of ₹5.75 crore to acquire additional equity shares in Saraswat Co-operative Bank.
Gufic Biosciences received 3 observations in Form FDA 483 following a USFDA pre-approval inspection at its Indore manufacturing facility.

watchlist.text: USFDA clearance of the Indore facility observations
